citation.authors: Bjornsson HK, Bjornsson ES, Avula B, Khan IA et al

cited_by.title: Ashwagandha: stress, sleep, thyroid and liver cautions

record.population: Five adults (mean age 43, three men) with liver injury attributed to ashwagandha supplements, from Iceland and the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network
record.design: Case series with structured expert causality assessment
record.finding: All five became jaundiced with nausea, lethargy, itching or abdominal discomfort after 2 to 12 weeks. The injury was cholestatic or mixed. Itching and raised bilirubin lasted 5 to 20 weeks, no one developed liver failure, and liver tests returned to normal within 1 to 5 months in four of the five.
record.note: A harm signal from five cases. It cannot say how often this happens. Not a trial.
